question.text: Mr. Karan Desai, LP in 'Konark Growth' Cat II AIF, has subscribed INR 50 crore and wants to co-invest in 'Saraswati Robotics', an investee where the AIF is investing INR 100 crore (Karan's pro-rata share via the fund = INR 10 crore). Under the 2025 CIV framework, what is the maximum co-investment Karan can make across CIV schemes in Saraswati Robotics (assuming Karan is not in an exempt category)?

answer.text: INR 10 crore (equal to his AIF share)
Unlimited, because accredited investors have no cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on Co-Investment Vehicles (pp. 311-312), the co-investments of an investor across CIV schemes in the same investee company shall not exceed three times that investor's contribution through the AIF scheme into that investee company. Karan's pro-rata contribution through the AIF in Saraswati Robotics is INR 10 crore, so the 3x cap permits a maximum co-investment of INR 30 crore. The source also lists certain investor categories that are exempt from this cap; Karan does not fall in those exempt categories. The Trap: INR 10 crore is the 1x amount equal to his AIF share. INR 20 crore is a 2x cap, which is not the source-supported multiple. Unlimited applies only to the exempt investor categories listed in the source, and the stem explicitly places Karan outside those categories. Note: The 3x cap in pp. 311-312 is computed on the investor's contribution through the AIF into the same investee company, and the exempt categories are limited to those expressly listed in the source.
